extracted.intended_audience: Assigned reviewers for ICCV 2023 (conference paper reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and practical instructions for performing peer review of ICCV 2023 submissions via the CMT system, including downloading papers, checking conflicts and submission-rule violations, writing/preparing reviews, participating in discussions, and entering final recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log into CMT and choose Reviewer role
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you've been notified by email that papers have been assigned to you, please log into the CMT site (https://cmt3.research.microsoft.com/ICCV2023), choose the “Reviewer” role on top, and follow the steps below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Download assigned papers and supplementary files
rubrics_metrics.description: Download your papers. To download individual papers, you can click the links underneath individual paper titles. Or, you can click the “Actions” button in the top right corner and then choose “Download Files.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using “Download Files” allows you to download a zip file containing all the papers plus supplementary files (if available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for conflicts of interest and submission-rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for possible conflict or submission rule violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Program Chairs (programchairs-iccv23@googlegroups.com) as well as your Area Chair (via CMT) immediately if you think you are conflicted with the paper (see “Avoid Conflict of Interest”) or you think the paper violates submission rules regarding anonymity, double submission, or plagiarism (refer to Author Guidelines for precise definitions). In the meantime, go ahead and review the paper as if there is no violation. The Program Chairs will follow up, but it may take a bit of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read Reviewer Guidelines before writing reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you start writing your reviews, make sure you have read the Reviewer Guidelines above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review papers and assign a preliminary (pre-rebuttal) rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Review papers and assign them a preliminary (pre-rebuttal) rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a paper, under the review column, click "Edit Review" to get to the review form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional: perform offline reviewing via Import/Export
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enable offline reviewing, go to “Actions -> Import Reviews”. You can select papers and click “Download” to obtain XML review stubs and the update files as needed. Once you are done updating, you can upload the file from the same page. We suggest that you use an XML editor to edit the file. You should always verify the review after uploading by inspecting it online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in discussions with Area Chairs and other reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: After the rebuttal period, reviewers will work with Area Chairs to clear up any confusions and attempt to reach consensus on papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CMT site has an electronic bulletin board feature that allows Area Chairs to contact reviewers anonymously. Once the Area Chair posts a note, reviewers will be notified and asked to log in to see the post and respond. The identities of the reviewers will be hidden from each other (but not from the Area Chair).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter your final (post-rebuttal) recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter your final (post-rebuttal) recommendation in CMT after the rebuttal period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may differ from your preliminary rating, and should reflect your judgment taking into account all the other reviews, the authors' rebuttal, and the discussion about the paper (if any).
